header: Meeting header: Date: 2026-03-04 14:00 UTC | Duration: 42 minutes | Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jenna Morales (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Cardinal - Procurement), Mohammed Rahman (Cardinal - CISO), Ava Chen (Cardinal - Legal), Darin Lee (Cardinal - VP Eng)
summary: Procurement-focused call to review MSA/DPA redlines, SLAs and pricing approval for a pilot. Redwood AE/SE went through commercial terms, SLA tiers, data handling and security attachments. Cardinal requested specific DPA language around data residency, encryption/KMS, and a 99.9% uptime SLA with credits. Action items: Redwood to send redlined MSA and pricing sheet; SE to share SOC2 and integration notes; Cardinal to return legal redlines and confirm pilot environment and SSO requirements.
topics: DPA: data residency, retention, deletion guarantees
SLA tiers, uptime SLOs, credits and remedies
Pricing: committed usage vs pay-as-you-go and pilot discounts
Technical pilot scope and benchmark requirements
transcript:
00:00 Speaker 1 (Samir): Alright good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. We know this is the procurement and legal review so we’ll keep it focused. I’m Samir, AE at Redwood, Jenna is our solutions engineer, um, and we’re here to walk through the MSA/DPA, SLAs and pricing for the pilot.
00:18 Speaker 2 (Lena): Hi Samir, thanks. We have the Cardinal team on, I’m Lena in procurement, Mohammed our CISO, Ava from legal, and Darin who’s leading engineering.
00:27 Speaker 3 (Mohammed): Hey all. Quick ask up front — we need to make sure any DPA language covers EU data residency for some of our customers, and KMS key control.
00:36 Speaker 1 (Samir): Yep, totally, that’s expected. Jenna will cover the security attachments, SOC 2, KMS notes. On the MSA side we’re flexible but want to capture a standard set of enterprise terms.
00:46 Speaker 4 (Jenna): Hi everyone. On the DPA — Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM and can run private deployments in a VPC for data residency. Our standard DPA includes deletion and retention windows, but we’re happy to look at specific wording.
00:59 Speaker 2 (Lena): Great. On pricing, procurement wants to understand committed capacity discounts vs pay-as-you-go and the timeline to sign.
01:06 Speaker 1 (Samir): For the pilot we usually do a time-boxed committed minimum — it gives a discount and priority capacity. We’d propose a 3-month pilot with a discounted commit and then roll to either dedicated or hosted depending on results.
01:18 Speaker 5 (Ava): Legally we’re looking at three items in the MSA: liability caps, IP carve-outs around customer prompts/outputs, and termination for convenience notice periods, also export control language.
01:30 Speaker 1 (Samir): Understood. On liability caps we mirror market norms, but we can discuss specific numbers. For IP: customer data and prompts remain customer-owned; model outputs are, uh, usually licensed back to the customer under the terms but we can clarify.
01:45 Speaker 3 (Mohammed): Also can you confirm retention — how long do you keep logs, prompts, and KV cache if we use hosted? We need to ensure we can opt for no retention for sensitive workloads.
01:58 Speaker 4 (Jenna): By default logs for hosted are retained for 30 days for debugging then purged; for regulated customers we have a no-retention mode and private deployment where logs never leave your VPC, and we can drop telemetry.
02:12 Speaker 2 (Lena): Okay good. On SLAs — we want a 99.9% uptime SLA and clarity on latency SLOs for our use case — customer support triage times, and credit structure.
02:24 Speaker 1 (Samir): We have SLA tiers: standard hosted SLA is 99.5%; enterprise dedicated can get to 99.9% with a financial credit ladder, and custom SLAs are possible in Private with reserved capacity. We'll include specific credits in the SLA attachment.
02:40 Speaker 5 (Ava): When you say credits, is that formulaic? We need a clear remedy table — % downtime mapping to % credit — and a maximum liability cap tied to the MSA.
02:51 Speaker 1 (Samir): Yes we use a table — e.g., <99.5% uptime: 10% credit, <99%: 25% credit — something like that; we’ll share the exact matrix. We also tie max credit to a portion of monthly fees as per the MSA.
03:06 Speaker 3 (Mohammed): Security controls: SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs. Also want to confirm network egress requirements — data egress and how it’s billed.
03:18 Speaker 4 (Jenna): SSO/SAML supported, RBAC via roles in the console, audit logs available with extended retention as an add-on. Egress billing depends on deployment: in our hosted multi-tenant egress is billed per GB, in dedicated or private it's typically included in the reserved capacity agreement — we can call that out in pricing.
03:36 Speaker 2 (Lena): Can you send the DPA template with the KMS language and the SOC 2 report? Procurement needs those to move to legal review.
03:44 Speaker 1 (Samir): Absolutely — Jenna will share SOC 2 and DPA template after the call.
03:49 Speaker 5 (Ava): On indemnity and export controls, we want to add a clause about logging access and audit rights for a subprocessor list.
03:58 Speaker 4 (Jenna): We maintain a subprocessor list and can include it in the DPA appendix; access to logs for audits can be arranged with appropriate NDAs — for private deployments it's straightforward since logs stay in your environment.
04:11 Speaker 1 (Samir): For the procurement timeline — what's your target go/no-go?
04:16 Speaker 2 (Lena): We’re aiming to approve pilot spend this month, vendor approval by mid-March ideally. Legal has to complete redlines in the next week or so.
04:25 Speaker 1 (Samir): Ok realistic. We’ll aim to get redlined MSA to you by Friday (2026-03-06) with updated pricing. That should give legal time to respond.
04:33 Speaker 5 (Ava): One more thing — SLAs around inference latency are important. Our product needs percentiles for tail latency — p95/p99 for 512-token workloads.
04:45 Speaker 4 (Jenna): We capture telemetry and can provide p50/p95/p99 for the pilot. For p99 at 512 tokens on shared hosted it's variable but with Dedicated or Private we can tune batch sizes and kernels for consistent p99. We can run benchmark reports during pilot.
05:02 Speaker 3 (Mohammed): Also encryption in transit and at rest — do you provide customer-managed keys for model context storage (KV cache)?
05:10 Speaker 4 (Jenna): Yes KMS support covers KV cache and storage; HSM options via our private deployment are available for higher-compliance customers.
05:19 Speaker 2 (Lena): Pricing detail — if we commit to X tokens/month for 3 months, what's the discount band? We need a table to show procurement.
05:28 Speaker 1 (Samir): We'll provide a pricing spreadsheet with commit tiers: 10% off for small commit, 20% for mid, 30%+ for larger enterprise commitments — exact thresholds in the spreadsheet. Pilot discounts also apply.
05:39 Speaker 5 (Ava): Are there termination fees if we switch after pilot? We want reasonable exit clauses.
05:44 Speaker 1 (Samir): Standard termination for convenience with 60 days notice, no exit fee for returning to other providers; for reserved capacity, early termination might incur a payout for unused committed fees, but we can put guardrails in the contract.
05:58 Speaker 6 (Darin): Technical q: for model versions — can we pin to a model and avoid automatic upgrades that might change output? Need versioning and rollback in the runtime.
06:07 Speaker 4 (Jenna): Yes you can pin model versions and we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback. We also surface model performance metrics in the console.
06:15 Speaker 3 (Mohammed): For regulatory audits, will you provide audit logs and attestations?
06:20 Speaker 4 (Jenna): SOC 2 report and penetration test summary are available under NDA; audit logs can be exported to your SIEM.
06:28 Speaker 2 (Lena): Ok can we talk about the pilot scope? Darin, what's required to validate for your team?
06:33 Speaker 6 (Darin): We need throughput and latency for peak periods, key use-case prompts, and an integration runbook for VPC peering and SSO. We also want to test model quality against our eval set and track cost per inference.
06:48 Speaker 1 (Samir): Good. We'll propose a pilot plan: 3 weeks of integration/setup, 4 weeks of benchmark/run — we can define KPIs: p99 latency target, throughput, cost per 1k tokens, and quality thresholds.
06:59 Speaker 3 (Mohammed): What about data residency for EU customers — can you guarantee processing and storage in an EU region?
07:05 Speaker 4 (Jenna): Yes, we can pin processing to an EU region in our hosted product or run a Private deployment inside your EU VPC. DPA will include region commitments.
07:15 Speaker 2 (Lena): Procurement question: payment terms — net 30? Or do you require upfront for reserved capacity?
07:21 Speaker 1 (Samir): Standard is net 30 for hosted; reserved capacity often requires a monthly or quarterly invoice and can be prepaid depending on the contract. We'll note that in the pricing sheet.
07:31 Speaker 5 (Ava): On the MSA redlines: we'll send a marked-up doc that includes our standard data processing clauses and a counterproposal to liability caps. Expect that by Monday.
07:40 Speaker 1 (Samir): Sounds good. We'll prioritize the MSA redlines once received.
07:44 Speaker 6 (Darin): Also, can you support a canary route to fallback model variants in case of regression during rollouts? We want automatic fallback to previous model if quality drops.
07:54 Speaker 4 (Jenna): Absolutely. Our rollout supports canary, A/B, and automatic rollback based on configured metrics.
08:02 Speaker 2 (Lena): Any competitors we should be aware of from your side?
08:06 Speaker 1 (Samir): Customers often evaluate against Anthropic, OpenAI, and AWS Bedrock for managed endpoints. We can highlight differences in latency and cost predictability.
08:16 Speaker 5 (Ava): For compliance attachments, we need a clear subprocessor list and a way to get advance notice if new subprocessors are added.
08:24 Speaker 4 (Jenna): We provide a subprocessors registry and can include notification commitments in the DPA appendix.
08:31 Speaker 2 (Lena): Good. If we can get SOC2, DPA, pricing, and redlined MSA this week, legal can turn quickly.
08:39 Speaker 1 (Samir): We’ll do that. Jenna will drop SOC2 and DPA; I will send pricing and redlined MSA.
08:45 Speaker 3 (Mohammed): One more security point — do you run model training on customer prompts? If not, we need that explicit.
08:53 Speaker 4 (Jenna): We do not train on customer prompts by default; training is a separate opt-in. We'll make that explicit in the DPA and MSA.
09:01 Speaker 2 (Lena): Perfect. Any open questions from Cardinal?
09:04 Speaker 6 (Darin): None at the moment, just need the integration runbook and pilot timeline.
09:09 Speaker 5 (Ava): No further legal questions for now.
09:12 Speaker 1 (Samir): Great. Quick recap and actions: Samir send pricing and redlined MSA by 2026-03-06; Jenna share SOC 2, DPA template and KMS notes by 2026-03-05; Cardinal returns legal redlines by 2026-03-09; Darin to confirm pilot env requirements by 2026-03-10; schedule tech walkthrough for next week.
09:34 Speaker 2 (Lena): Ok thanks everyone.
09:36 Speaker 1 (Samir): Thanks all, we'll follow up via email and add action items to the CRM. Bye.
09:40 End of call
